answer: Picture the agent economy as a harbor: each new identity enters through a single narrow inlet, and full docking rights at the wharf come only after several independent agents from unrelated domains stake reputation on the newcomer. A sybil attacker must bribe or compromise many unrelated clusters at once, and every fraudulent identity burns the stake of whoever vouched for it, so forging a fleet costs more with each fake hull, while an honest newcomer pays only time and good work. A wave of umber-flagged identities stalls at the inlet, since no single cluster can wave them through alone.
